newsitem.title: FRANCE: Search for Canadian yachtsman suspended - French tv.
newsitem.headline: Search for Canadian yachtsman suspended - French tv.

text.p: The search for a Canadian yachtsman missing in the dramatic Vendee Globe sailing challenge has been temporarily suspended, French television said on Sunday.

France-3 television said a cargo vessel and another competitor who had gone to search for Gerry Roufs who has not been heard of since Tuesday left the area after a fruitless hunt in icy Antarctic seas roughly halfway between New Zealand and the bottom of South America.
The area is too far from dry land for the Australian air force, which dramatically rescued two other competitors in the race, to intervene, the television station said.
Another vessel was heading for the area to resume the search but it is not expected to begin scouring the seas where he was last heard from until later on Sunday, France-3 said.

A reconnaissance satellite has also been programmed to look out for Roufs but officials of the French-organised race say they believe it has only an outside chance of being useful in the huge area it must cover.
The Australian naval vessel HMAS Adelaide was meanwhile heading home with two yachtsmen its helicopter plucked from the sea after they were spotted by Australian planes after several days at sea.
Briton Tony Bullimore, 56, was rescued on Thursday after surviving for four days in an air pocket in his upturned yacht, battered by high seas 2,600 km (1,600 miles) from Australia.
The Adelaide also rescued French yachtsman Thierry Dubois, a competitor in the same race.
The yachts of both Dubois and Bullimore capsized in heavy weather.

An Australian air force Orion maritime aircraft saved another race competitor, Frenchman Raphael Dinelli, on December 27 when it found him and dropped a life raft a few minutes before his overturned yacht sank.
The French government, whose 1995 nuclear bomb tests generated great hostility among Pacific nations, thanked Australia for the rescue.

An Orion found Dubois on Monday on his overturned yacht. As another Orion found Bullimore's boat -- with Bullimore inside, as it turned out -- the Australian navy dispatched the frigate at full speed to rescue the pair, who were well beyond usual merchant shipping lanes.
Orion aircraft watched over the two boats for three days until the ship picked up Dubois early on Thursday and then steamed on to Bullimore's yacht to discover him alive inside.
